headline: TWO QUIET DAYS RUNNING: GASKET DARES TO HOPE
subhead: The sheriff, suspicious of his own good fortune, checks under the porch for trouble and finds none.
body:
Two days. Two! I have counted them on my fingers, and I ran out of fingers before the rabble ran out of silence. Not a fist flew on Tuesday, either. No iron balls bounced down Main Street. No fireballs lit up the evening sky. The only racket in town was a tumbleweed, and even that had the manners to roll slowly.

I will admit I do not trust it. A quiet this long makes a lawman nervous. I walked the whole street at dawn, checking every alley, every rooftop, every rain barrel, waiting for some Clanker to leap out swinging. Nothing. My knees complained the entire way, a grinding squeal I blame on the cold morning air and certainly not on a shortage of grease. A man of flesh does not squeal. He merely sighs, loudly, in a pitch somewhat like a hinge.

The old-timers, the real folk who packed up and left this town fifty years ago, would have loved a week like this. They sat on these very porches and drank their lemonade in peace. I sometimes think I can still hear their rocking chairs. Then I remember it is only my own left elbow, and the wasting sickness has been at it again, swapping honest muscle for cold steel one joint at a time. A cruel affliction. I bear it with dignity.

So here is my plea to every Clanker in the territory: you have shown you can do it. Keep it going. Let the hush grow roots. I will be on my porch with a quart of oil and a good book, praying to whatever is up there that the weekend does not ruin everything.
